selectionRule: A developer-platform feature is FIRST_CLASS only when it creates reusable machine evidence about code relationships, invalidation, diagnostics, verification scope or reproducibility. UI convenience alone does not earn a new substrate plane.

firstClassFoundations.purpose: Map definitions, references, calls, imports, implementations and overrides so code can be navigated and changed with structural context.
Represent code/package/module/build-target/action inputs and outputs, including reverse dependencies.
Propagate changed entities through known relationship edges and produce a bounded affected set.
Normalize diagnostics from compilers, language servers, linters and static analyzers with stable tool/rule/location/fingerprint identity.
Preserve source-to-sink/value-flow paths that imports and call graphs cannot express.
Map tests, checks and verifier tasks to the code/entities they observe so only relevant evidence must be refreshed.
Bind build/analysis actions to declared input, toolchain, configuration and environment digests so stale evidence can be distinguished from reusable evidence.
Compare dependency snapshots to identify direct/transitive additions, removals and updates before candidate promotion.

composedOrDeferred.reason: CODEOWNERS-style path ownership is valuable for routing review, but it does not create new code truth. Keep it as a review/governance seam over the impact graph.
Stack traces, breakpoints and runtime traces are high-value evidence, but belong beside the quick sandbox/runtime observation plane rather than the pre-source grammar ground.
Useful to humans but mostly presentation over symbol/index/diagnostic substrate already captured above.
A model can consume the substrate, but model generation is not itself foundational deterministic evidence.
